metadata.note: The Virginia Blue Ridge Railway (incorporated 22 May 1914), an independent common-carrier short line built 1915-16 for the Tye River Timber Co. and Leftwich Timber Co. sawmills, from a junction with the Southern Railway's Washington - Lynchburg main line at Tye River, Nelson County, up the Piney River valley to Massies Mill (16 mi; Piney River at 7 mi). Mixed trains carried passengers from 1916; the date they stopped is disputed (see not_yet_sourced). Freight - titanium (Southern Mineral Products / American Cyanamid) and aplite - kept it going until embargo in 1980; rails salvaged 1985. The grade is now partly the Blue Ridge Railway Trail. Independent throughout: no lease, merger or operating agreement, so no ownership split.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules eff. Sept 1951), VBR entry 'Operated for freight service only' and station-index daggers (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 122862-122880, 311508-311515, 327566-327567, 333076)

not_yet_sourced: pax_end of the Tye River - Massies Mill mixed train: drawn to 1917 [OPEN] (last year before the dated Dec 1917 - Nov 1918 shutdown). Sources say 1920 at the latest (Farm Collector memoir, eyewitness), 1936 (Whippany, american-rails, Don's Depot, virginiaplaces -- probably one lineage), 1937 (unnamed newspaper), 1939 (Wikipedia). Hard ceiling: Feb 1952 Official Guide, freight only. Settle with Official Guide listings 1920/1925/1930/1935, the ICC valuation report for the VBR, the UVA Special Collections VBR business archives (viu01221) or a Lynchburg/Amherst newspaper 'last train' story.
Whether mixed-train service resumed after the line reopened in Nov 1918 -- no source checked confirms any passenger year 1918-1956.
pax_start 1915 vs 1916: a June 1915 Times-Dispatch item reports a planned passenger service; only Whippany's 1916 is a dated start.
How far past Piney River the 19 May 1957 charter ran ('to the aplite mines') -- not drawn.
Mileage: Times-Dispatch (June 1915) implies 22 mi and a UVA finding aid ~19 mi against the Guide's and Whippany's 16 mi; traced 16 mi was the target.
All headways and speeds are estimates.
branches_deliberately_omitted: [3] Junction - Woodson (c.4 mi lumber spur to the Woodson Lumber Co. mill, opened Oct 1915; track lifted c.1924-25 per Whippany or abandoned 1939 per virginiaplaces/ICC): drawable NONE -- no source puts a passenger or mixed train on it.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn: the whole road from the end of mixed-train service to embargo 1 July 1980 (and the final moves to 6 April 1985), apart from the two dated railfan charters; 1958 and 1960-1985 are freight only. The Woodson spur is excluded.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced Tye River - Roses Mill - Piney River - Massies Mill on the old_railway_operator=Virginia Blue Ridge Railway grade in OSM: 15.2 mi traced against 16 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide). No straight-line legs; about 0.2 mi is opstrace graph connectors bridging OSM way ends that do not share a node. Waypoints were placed on the tagged grade itself (Tye River junction at the east end of way 700715255, 42 m from the NS Washington District; Piney River 0.32 km from the hamlet geocode; Massies Mill at the north end of way 19847773, 0.24 km from the hamlet geocode). Traced is 5% under the documented 16 mi; the OSM grade may omit terminal trackage at either end. Lowesville (pinned by hand: Nominatim returned Lowesville Road) lies 1.4 km off the drawn grade; Roses Mill was hand-pinned on the grade (Nominatim found nothing). An extra waypoint at the grade's bend north of Piney River (end of way 1426866148) keeps the Piney River - Massies Mill leg from tripping the 1.6x chord rule; it is not identified with the station called Junction. The grade is the road's only alignment (built 1915-16, lifted 1985), so no later-alignment issue; the exact Tye River connection track to the Southern is not mapped and the line stops at the grade's end beside the main line.

segments.note: Mixed-train passenger service, Tye River (junction with the Southern Railway) - Roses Mill - Piney River - Lowesville - Massies Mill, with one second-hand wooden combination baggage/passenger car with a segregated section. Start: the Whippany Railway Museum history says passenger service 'was started in 1916 with one combination baggage / passenger car' (a June 1915 Richmond Times-Dispatch item only reports a planned passenger service). The line was shut down Dec 1917 - Nov 1918 when its sawmills were declared non-essential (Whippany), so the drawn span stops at 1917. END CONFLICT, UNRESOLVED: a first-hand Farm Collector memoir says passenger service ended '1920 at the latest' (the combine lasted to about 1925, then became a caboose) and disputes a newspaper's 1937; Whippany, american-rails.com and Don's Depot say 1936; an unnamed newspaper (cited in the memoir) says 1937; Wikipedia ('Tye River') says 1939, apparently misciting Don's Depot. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules Sept 1951) lists the road as freight only. The drawn end, 1917, is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: it is the year before the dated wartime shutdown, the only point before which service is implied by a sourced start. Whether mixed trains resumed after Nov 1918, and for how long, is not proven by any source checked -- do not extend to 1936 or any other year without a timetable or ICC/company record. Freight continued after passengers ended (titanium and aplite traffic from 1931/1935) until embargo 1 July 1980; last move 6 April 1985. Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed; by 1926 trains ran only three days a week).
sources: Segment-level: start year 1916 and the Dec 1917 - Nov 1918 wartime shutdown from the Whippany Railway Museum history (pp.1-4); the end-year conflict from the Farm Collector memoir, Whippany, american-rails.com, Don's Depot and the Feb 1952 Official Guide as named in the note. The 1916-1917 span itself rests on one secondary source; the headway is unsourced.

segments.note: One-day railfan charter, 19 May 1957: the VBR's first railfan excursion, chartered by the Washington D.C. Chapter NRHS, a baggage car and six Southern Railway coaches run through off the Southern at Tye River, then on past Piney River 'west to the aplite mines' (terminus unstated, not drawn). A single charter, not a service; the headway is nominal. ANCHOR: this one year is proven; nothing ran in 1958.
sources: Segment-level: date, charterer and consist from the Whippany Railway Museum history p.5.

segments.note: One-day NRHS 'Photographer's Special', 21 June 1959: riders on benches in two gondolas plus a caboose, two trips Piney River - Tye River behind engine No. 8; Whippany calls it 'the last full-fledged fan trip' the VBR ran. A single charter, not a service; the headway is nominal. ANCHOR: this one year is proven. Later informal rides on a track car or caboose are undated and not drawn; a 1964 proposal for commercial steam tourist trains in 1965 never ran.
sources: Segment-level: date, equipment and extent from the Whippany Railway Museum history p.6 (and p.7 on later proposals); Crozet Gazette photo caption confirms the June 1959 NRHS Washington chapter excursion with No. 8 at Piney River.
